# temps_environment_ingress (Resource)

How the Temps proxy admits traffic to an environment: `legacy` keeps the old behaviour, `shadow` evaluates the new rules without enforcing them, `enforce` applies them; `require_login` puts the environment behind Temps sign-in.

Destroying the resource leaves the settings as they are; it only stops managing them.

Import with `<project_id>/<environment_id>`.

Required API key permissions: `environments:read`, `environments:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_environment_ingress" "staging" {
  project_id     = temps_project.web.id
  environment_id = temps_environment.staging.id
  mode           = "enforce"
  require_login  = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (Number) ID of the environment.
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.

### Optional

- `mode` (String) Ingress mode. One of `legacy`, `shadow`, `enforce`.
- `require_login` (Boolean) Require visitors to sign in to Temps.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID, `<project_id>/<environment_id>`.
- `login_enforced` (Boolean) Whether sign-in is enforced now.
- `login_permission` (String) Permission a visitor needs once signed in.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id>/<environment_id>
terraform import temps_environment_ingress.staging 8/21
```
